reasons: All of B's slogans rest on English senses of 'baton' (club, relay baton, conductor's baton) that Russian «батон» does not have, so the jokes would not land for Russian readers, and B wrongly claims they are a Russian mechanism. A has at least one real Russian sound play («Батя на районе», батон/батя) that fits a neighbourhood sign, although several of its other slogans are weak or make little sense («Батон, а не батон», «Батон, который передают»). B's 'не бьёт' and 'не будильник' slogans also fit a bakery sign poorly.

A: Claims «Батон, который передают» has a relay-baton double meaning, but Russian «батон» is not a relay baton.
B: Claims Russian «батон» also means a club or stick ('дубина'), a relay baton and a conductor's baton; these are English senses of 'baton', and Russian uses «палочка»/«дубинка» for them.
